Quantitative CT Perfusion Enhancement Metrics for Differentiating Solid Renal Tumors

Sara Babapour, Jouan Taheri Talesh, Grace Li, Luke Phan, Brian Chau, and 1 more

This is a preprint; it has not been peer reviewed by a journal.

https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-9581498/v1

This work is licensed under a CC BY 4.0 License

Abstract
Purpose

Among kidney solid lesions in which neovascularity carries a procedural risk, and benign tumors are prone to overdiagnosis and overtreatment, measurable thresholds may provide reproducible biomarkers to improve diagnostic classification non-invasively. Quantitative contrast distribution metrics, derived from CT perfusion (CTp), were assessed to reflect the solid tumor cytology character.

Method

In this retrospective IRB-approved, HIPAA-compliant study, patients with pathologically confirmed renal masses who underwent CTp imaging prior to interventions were included. Volumes of interest (VOI) were drawn on the most enhancing portion of the mass, ipsilateral and contralateral kidney cortex, after window level adjustments. Maximum HU values relative to wash-in at 0.0 seconds of tissue contrast penetration were obtained on Syngo Via-generated (SH, Malvern, PA) virtually reconstructed image. Relative perfusion parameters of VOI, such as flow extraction (FE), and time to peak (TTP), were compared by a two-sided paired sample t-test between tumors and contralateral cortex and presented as perfusion curves.

Results

A total of 80 target renal lesions were analyzed (ccRCC: N = 44; pRCC: N = 14; oncocytoma: N = 16; Chromophobe: N = 6). Distinctive relative peak wash-in thresholds (HU) for malignant lesions, ccRCC and pRCC (p < 0.003; ccRCC-to-cortex > 0.92; pRCC-to-aorta < 0.47) with distinct shorter TTP, or greater peak enhancement for ccRCC were observed compared to healthy cortex (P < 0.016). However, both aggressive chromophobe and ccRCC tumors with neovascularity showed overlapping values. Meanwhile, oncocytomas intermediate and indolent enhancement characteristics were presented with distinct washout profiles.

Conclusion

Time- relative enhancement parameters of ccRCC, pRCC are distinctive, and the indolent wash-in curves of benign solid lesions demonstrated remarkable differences in certain hemodynamic parameters.
